correctness.rationale: Prime-by-prime valuation of tau(n)=product(a_i+1) gives the exact exponent-matrix criterion. The count of S-smooth shifted exponents is an elementary simplex lattice count. Upper and lower product boxes have the same leading constant, and any failure of the column inequalities forces at least one shifted exponent into an O(log log x) boundary set, whose cardinality is o((log log x)^(m^2)). Finite replay confirms the exact criterion but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The theorem decomposes a classical sparse integer sequence by any prescribed exact prime support and produces an explicit, support-dependent leading constant with exponent m^2. The exact exponent-matrix criterion also gives a direct structural description. This is an infinite distribution theorem with a natural arithmetic interpretation, not a routine finite computation.
